New York —
Morgan Stanley announced Ted Pick will serve as its new CEO starting January 1, succeeding long-serving head James Gorman.
Gorman will become executive chairman, the bank announced Wednesday.
Pick had served as co-president of Morgan Stanley for the past two years, the company said. He’s a veteran at the banking giant, also overseeing investment banking, equities, fixed income, capital markets and research. He also co-heads firm strategy. Pick first joined Morgan Stanley in 1990.
Gorman had announced in May he would [step down as the company’s CEO](https://www.cnn.com/2023/05/19/business/morgan-stanley-james-gorman-stepping-down/index.html) within the next 12 months, ending his tenure as one of the longest-serving heads of a US bank. He became CEO of Morgan Stanley in January 2010.

keenable.title: Ted Pick
keenable.snippet: Ted Pick, who spent his entire career at Morgan Stanley, [became the investment bank’s 11th CEO in January 2024](https://fortune.com/2023/10/26/who-morgan-stanleys-new-ceo-ted-pick-the-bank-veteran-succeed-james-gorman/). Pick rose through the ranks after starting as an analyst in 1990; later came a promotion to managing director, and he was named to the investment bank’s management committee in 2008. Ted Pick is an American banker who serves as Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Morgan Stanley. He has held the CEO role since January 2024 and assumed the chairmanship in January 2025, succeeding James Gorman.

He is the quintessential Wall Street insider — a man who joined Morgan Stanley as an analyst in 1990, spent more than three decades mastering every dimension of the bank's institutional business, and ultimately ascended to its highest office as Chairman and Chief Executive Officer. Since taking the CEO role on January 1, 2024, and adding the chairmanship in January 2025, Pick has assumed leadership of one of the world's most prestigious financial institutions at a moment of both significant opportunity and meaningful competitive challenge.

Born in New York City in 1968, Pick grew up partly in Caracas, Venezuela, before returning to the United States for his education. He studied Russian history and politics at Middlebury College — a seemingly unconventional foundation for a career in global finance — before earning an MBA from Harvard Business School. His intellectual eclecticism, combined with a lifelong passion for Morgan Stanley, has produced a leader known for his intensity, loyalty, client focus, and deep institutional knowledge.

Pick is credited with transforming Morgan Stanley's equities business into the global market leader, engineering a critical turnaround of the firm's fixed income division, and helping raise capital during the 2008 financial crisis that brought the firm to the edge of collapse. Morgan Stanley named Ted Pick as its next CEO on Wednesday, ending a years-long, three-way race to succeed James Gorman atop the bank.
Pick, head of Morgan Stanley’s institutional securities group — which encompasses investment banking, equities, fixed income, capital markets and research — will take over as CEO on Jan. 1, at which point Gorman will become the bank’s executive chair for an unspecified time.
Gorman launched Morgan Stanley’s succession sweepstakes in 2021, with a raft of promotions that boosted the profile of the three finalists, as well as Jon Pruzan, the bank’s now-former chief operating officer who left in January to ultimately become president of the investment firm Pretium. Gorman in May, put a timeline on his departure, saying he’d step down within 12 months. The outgoing CEO described Pick on Wednesday as someone who “is battle-tested.”
In Pick, Morgan Stanley chooses a 33-year veteran of the bank. He started in 1990 as an analyst, then rose equity capital markets to run that business in 2005. He moved to global equities trading in 2009 and ascended in 2015 to global head of sales and trading, where he reportedly cut fixed-income staff by 25%, yet still increased revenues. Pick had reportedly long been seen as the front-running CEO candidate.
